findings.title: GitHub user check is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, the view returns `pipeline.next_step()` without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to anyone. That happens whenever the installation webhook has not arrived or been processed yet. `build_integration` then fetches the installation with the app JWT and creates the integration for whatever `installation_id` was supplied in the query string. Someone who knows another account's installation_id can win this race and bind that GitHub installation to their own Sentry org, which is the attack this PR is meant to stop. The installer identity should be checked in this branch too, for example by comparing against the installation's sender or account from the GitHub API, or the step should fail closed.

findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata has no `sender`
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every existing Integration has a `sender` entry. `build_integration` only sets it when `state.get("sender")` is present, and older integrations or ones created through other paths may not have it. In those cases this line raises an uncaught KeyError, and the user gets a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and treat a missing sender as a failed check.

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions in the OAuth token exchange and user lookup
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` on line 423 is outside the try block, so network or connection errors propagate. The HTTP status of the response is never checked. `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` raises an API error when GitHub returns a non-2xx response, for example a revoked token or rate limiting. All of these escape `dispatch` as a 500 instead of rendering the 'Invalid installation request' error page that the PR says users will see in these cases.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL is built without URL-encoding parameters
findings.body: `redirect_uri` is an absolute URL containing `:` and `/` characters, and `client_id` and `state` are interpolated raw into the query string. If the configured URL prefix ever contains `?`, `&`, `#` or similar characters, the query string to GitHub will be malformed. Build it with `urlencode({...})`.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests a missing installation
findings.body: The test now sends a `state` (`ddd023...`) that does not match the pipeline signature. It therefore fails at the state check in OAuthLoginView and never reaches `build_integration`. The 404 branch ('The GitHub installation could not be found.') is no longer covered. Use the correct state value and restore the original assertion. Add a separate test for the state-mismatch case.
